display.title: Tu B'Shvat: The Trees Say Happy New Year
display.summary_short: On Tu B'Shvat, the New Year for Trees, Uncle Yossi pictures the trees wishing each other a happy new year and explains why we eat new fruits of Eretz Yisroel.
display.summary_long: A short Tu B'Shvat greeting from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, recorded on the eve of the fifteenth of Shevat. Uncle Yossi asks children to stretch their imagination and hear the trees and fruits wishing one another 'L'shanah tovah', because Tu B'Shvat is Rosh Hashanah La'ilanos, the New Year for Trees. We celebrate by eating fruits, especially those that grow in Eretz Yisroel and those we have not yet eaten this year, so that we can say the brachah Borei Pri Ha'etz and also Shehecheyanu. He wishes everyone a hearty appetite and blesses them that the new year bring good fruits of their own: good deeds and good character, more Torah learning and more mitzvos than ever before.
display.lesson: Like the trees, we should bring forth good fruits: good deeds, good midos, more Torah and more mitzvos.
